clue.text: The virtuous aren't found in police force

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi police and paramilitary force
ain't is the colloquial form of aren't

explanation.surface: A cynical remark that no good people are to be found among the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The SS (Hitler's police force) holds AINT. Southampton FC are nicknamed the Saints, one of many club nicknames in this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Saints are people of exceptional goodness, so collectively they are the virtuous.

clue.text: Kane, perhaps on the left, is encouraged

parts.note: Harry Kane played for Tottenham Hotspur, whose players are Spurs
left-wing politics is described as red

explanation.surface: The striker Harry Kane, playing on the left wing, is given encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur, nicknamed Spurs, are a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur a horse on is to urge it forward, hence to encourage.

clue.text: Playmaker with affliction in hip

indicators.note: in says the disease goes within the fashionable word

parts.note: hip means fashionable, which is in
BSE is mad cow disease, an affliction

explanation.surface: A midfield playmaker suffers a hip injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playmaker' is football talk for a creative midfielder, but here it means a maker of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian dramatist wrote plays such as A Doll's House, so he made plays.

clue.text: Row about blunder, one foxes may avoid?

indicators.note: about means around, so the row wraps round the blunder

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
to err is to blunder

explanation.surface: A row breaks out about a mistake made by someone foxes would steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: Terriers were bred to chase foxes from their dens, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog bred for going to earth after foxes is one foxes would sensibly shun.

clue.text: Pack, card player works out, lacking spades

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, so W is a card player

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for works out

parts.note: to work out a problem is to solve it
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player in a pack-and-cards game figures out a hand without any spades.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S from SOLVES and put W in front. Wolverhampton Wanderers are nicknamed Wolves.
explanation.definitionFit: Wolves hunt together in a group known as a pack, so the animals collectively make one.

clue.text: Looking annoyed, wanting power trip

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: pouting is pushing out the lips in annoyance
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A sulky person is denied a power trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power trip' reads as one phrase but power is the letter removed.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is a short excursion, a jaunt or day trip.

clue.text: Drink abroad and get out lots of drink for game

parts.note: vin is French for wine

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of get are rearranged

parts.note: a tun is a large cask holding a great deal of drink

explanation.surface: Someone drinks wine abroad then brings out plenty more for a party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges GET into GTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vingt-et-un, French for twenty-one, is the card game also called pontoon or blackjack.

clue.text: Flyer nearly cheeks fool

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: the cheeks of the backside are the seat
to gull someone is to fool them

explanation.surface: A cheeky aviator almost fools someone.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAT loses its T. Brighton and Hove Albion are the Seagulls.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is a seabird, and any bird is a flyer.

clue.text: Learner's cracking debut fit for top clubs

indicators.note: cracking means breaking into, so the learner goes inside the debut

parts.note: a premiere is a first performance, a debut
L is the learner-driver plate
an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: A young learner's breakthrough debut makes them fit for the big clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cracking' means the learner's letter breaks into the debut just before its final letter. 'fit' looks like fitness for the top clubs, but is a bout of fever.
explanation.definitionFit: England's top football division is the Premier League, made up of the leading clubs.

clue.text: Arsenal may display these tight turns

indicators.note: turns tells us to read the word for tight from back to front

parts.note: a snug fit is a tight one

explanation.surface: A football commentary on Arsenal playing tight and twisting play.
explanation.walkthrough: SNUG read backwards. Arsenal FC are the Gunners and have a cannon on their badge; an arsenal is also a store of weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a weapons store, which might well show off firearms, and the club badge pictures a cannon.

clue.text: Train in a ground after game in a fantastic country

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

indicators.note: ground means crushed or broken up, so the letters of train in a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A train passes through a sports ground after a match, somewhere far-fetched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges the letters of 'Train in a'. The definition is adjectival: Ruritania is the invented kingdom of The Prisoner of Zenda.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things belonging to Ruritania, an imaginary Central European kingdom from fiction.

clue.text: Country Britain governed that is overthrown

parts.note: B is an abbreviation for Britain, as in GB
to run a country is to govern it

indicators.note: overthrown turns the abbreviation for that is upside down, reading it backwards in an across light

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A colonial history: a country Britain once ruled that has since been toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrown' turns IE into EI at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sultanate on Borneo, a former British protectorate and an independent nation.

clue.text: New trio with Man United's legendary menace

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United in club names

explanation.surface: Three new signings for Manchester United are being hyped as a fearsome threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges TRIOMANU. Man U is the common short name for Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: The bull-headed monster of Greek myth in the Cretan labyrinth was a menace from legend.

clue.text: Notice reporter half-cut before his boss retired

indicators.note: before places the shortened word ahead of the boss

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

indicators.note: half-cut, usually meaning tipsy, here says only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: a reporter is a journalist
a journalist's boss is the editor, ED

explanation.surface: A tipsy reporter files notice of retirement before his editor does.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' leaves JOURN, the first half of JOURNALIST. Retired here means withdrew, as a court adjourns to another room.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjourned means broke off and withdrew, as people retire to another room after dinner.

clue.text: The powerful old girl working with cash

indicators.note: working means being put to work and changed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful elderly woman is busy with her money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges GIRLCASH into LIGARCHS, after O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oligarchs are the small group of rich, influential people who wield control, so the powerful.

clue.text: Former backs and the like

indicators.note: backs says the word for former runs in reverse

parts.note: the late president is the former one

explanation.surface: Talk of former full-backs and similar players.
explanation.walkthrough: LATE read backwards gives the Latin abbreviation et al.
explanation.definitionFit: Et al, from Latin et alii, means and others, used to cut a list short.

clue.text: Lofted ball in, after header from Chelsea

indicators.note: after places the fashionable word behind the initial
the header of a word is its first letter, here taken from the club name

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is hip

explanation.surface: A lofted ball comes in for a Chelsea player to head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' is football misdirection: it means the first letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: In football and golf a chip is a short shot that lifts the ball into the air.

clue.text: County towns content to leave drinks

parts.note: Clare is a county in the west of Ireland

indicators.note: removing a word's content leaves only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Country town residents are happy to leave once the drinks run out.
explanation.walkthrough: TOWNS with its inside removed leaves TS. Burnley are nicknamed the Clarets.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine, so clarets are drinks.

clue.text: Team — this one's left in small pieces?

parts.note: a football or cricket side is an eleven

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the letter for one goes out of the word

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone muses on a team that has been left in pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's left' means I has gone from THIS, leaving THS. The question mark flags that elevenths are only modest fractions.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of eleven equal parts of a whole is a fairly small fraction.

clue.text: Frankly, nothing stops Com-munist guerrillas with China

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so nothing goes inside the guerrillas

parts.note: VC is the Viet Cong, the Vietnamese communist guerrillas
O is the figure zero, nothing
in rhyming slang china plate means mate, an ally

explanation.surface: An outspoken remark that no communist rebels have Chinese backing.
explanation.walkthrough: China (capitalised) looks like the country, but is rhyming slang: china plate means mate. The hyphen in Com-munist is only a line break.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking vocally means speaking out openly, so frankly.

clue.text: Men score, cutting through Harlequins' sides, or Wasps

indicators.note: cutting through means passing into, so these pieces go between the outer letters
the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: OR is other ranks, enlisted men
to net a goal is to score

explanation.surface: Rugby talk: players score by breaking through the Harlequins defence, or that of Wasps.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequins and Wasps are English rugby clubs, but here wasps are insects; Watford FC are the Hornets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornets are large species of wasp, so they are wasps.

clue.text: One hoarding shows enchanting fellow clothing Greek character

indicators.note: clothing means dressing round, so the wizard wraps the Greek letter

parts.note: a mage is a magician, a man who casts spells
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A collector shows off a charming man's Greek-lettered outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enchanting' suggests charm but means casting spells. Newcastle United are the Magpies.
explanation.definitionFit: Magpies are said to collect shiny objects, so a magpie is a person who hoards things.

clue.text: Ruler knocked back a drink with a poor player

indicators.note: knocked back, as with a drink downed, says everything after it reads in reverse

parts.note: a jar is a drink, especially of beer
a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: A ruler downs a drink in the company of an untalented actor.
explanation.walkthrough: A JAR A HAM written backwards. 'knocked back' looks like part of the drinking picture but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja is a great Indian prince, a hereditary ruler of a state.

clue.text: Ruddy track by female pop star

indicators.note: by places the railway beside the singer

parts.note: Cher is the American singer known by one name
RY abbreviates railway, a track

explanation.surface: A song track recorded by a woman pop singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bournemouth are the Cherries.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry as an adjective is a bright red, as in cherry-red lips or ruddy cheeks.

clue.text: English and Scots off target, mostly low score

indicators.note: mostly means not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: agley is Scots for awry, as in Burns's best-laid schemes that gang aft agley

explanation.surface: English and Scottish golfers miss the target, mostly with low scores.
explanation.walkthrough: AGLEY loses its Y. Crystal Palace are the Eagles.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an eagle is two strokes under par on a hole, a low score.

clue.text: Interpretative psychologist's opening up Electra complex

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
complex means intricate and tangled, so the letters of up and Electra are rearranged

explanation.surface: A psychologist starts to explain the Electra complex, a Freudian theory of daughters and fathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges UPELECTRA into ERCEPTUAL, after P. 'Electra complex' reads as one psychological term but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Perceptual concerns how the mind takes in and makes sense of what the senses report.

clue.text: Unrestrained woman, one who's finished losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter is dropped

parts.note: a goner is someone who is doomed or done for

explanation.surface: A wild woman is beaten and has lost her spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: GONER without its central N.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a goer is a woman thought to be sexually adventurous, so unrestrained.

clue.text: Check on Saturday's clothing arrangement

indicators.note: on in an across light places the check after the outer letters
the clothing of a word is its outside letters, which wrap the rest

parts.note: to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: Checking on the arrangement of someone's Saturday outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer letters of Saturday are S and Y, and STEM follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised scheme or set-up, an ordered way things are put together.

clue.text: Solution's to keep City back, the French learn here

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: lye is an alkaline solution; with the possessive it gives the letters lyes

indicators.note: back says the postcode is read in reverse

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: A cleaning solution keeps a city clean while French people go to class.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the financial district of London, whose postcodes begin EC; 'back' turns that round before 'to keep' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lycée is a French secondary school, where French pupils study.
